answer: A haven for honest agents can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may transact, like a lotus that only opens after its roots take hold: the stake is slashed on proven fraud, and reputation accrues slowly from completed, attested work. An attacker spinning up a dune of fake identities must fund every one separately, so forging a thousand Sybils costs a thousand stakes while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
